briefs.task:
Plan the rest of Thrum's road to delivering the engine, as a project-level plan that brings water and clouds into it.

Purpose. The owner wants work lined up continuously toward the V1 exit in docs/BUILD-PLAN.md, so builders always have a next milestone, and wants water and clouds finished and consolidated. Today only PLATFORM-RUNTIME-MAC M2 and APPLE-TILE (G3t) are planned and open; everything after them is unplanned.

Water and clouds are built in the Broadsides repository at /Users/ryannel/Workspace/Broadsides, not here. Water is on branch codex/water-rust-system, with notes/water/DESIGN.md, DESIGN-PLAN.md and HANDOFF.md. Three spikes on 10 November left results on branches claude/fable-hull-release, claude/fable-near-waterline and claude/fable-foam (notes/water/FABLE-*.md on each). Two cloud paths, a baked library and a procedural one, were built by separate Codex agents in Broadsides; find their branches and notes there. docs/design/decisions/SEA-AND-CLOUD-PORT.md governs bringing them into Thrum: it says Thrum wasn't ready on 6 November and that the owner schedules porting. The owner has now asked for both to be finished and consolidated. Decide, with reasons, what finished means for each, whether that finishing happens in Broadsides first or as Thrum modules, and where in the build order the port's readiness conditions are met.

Done means: the project plan (module map, build order, contracts and a brief per module) covers the remaining work to the V1 exit plus water and clouds; each module that can start next has its design, plan and done-when file, so a builder can start it; and the build plan's active section points to it. List anything that needs an owner decision, such as port timing or spending, in your result rather than deciding it.

Boundaries. Don't change the definitions of PLATFORM-RUNTIME-MAC M2 or APPLE-TILE, because builders are on them. Read Broadsides but don't change it.
Revise ATMOSPHERE's design and plan as docs/evidence/ATMOSPHERE/design-review.md asks
Revise ATMOSPHERE's design and plan as docs/evidence/ATMOSPHERE/design-review.md asks

Unblock ATMOSPHERE M5: H2 fails its Metal precision bound. Current main retains the design instruction requiring a planner decision on this measured miss. Evidence: docs/evidence/ATMOSPHERE/m5-h2-blocker.md

The owner, 14 Nov 2026: "Oh and for clouds we also need to be taking into account mist / fog. We want a plan that's able to deliver on top quality atmosphere." Revise the plans so Thrum's atmosphere reaches the quality of shipped high-end games as a whole: sky, clouds, haze, and mist and fog (ground fog, valley mist, fog banks over water, low cloud the camera can enter), lit consistently and changing with the weather and time of day. Settle from first principles which module owns what across CLOUDS, ATMOSPHERE and any other affected module, keep one authority for each kind of state, and revise their designs, plans and done-when files. Broadsides is evidence, not a constraint. CLOUDS M1 is being built now; if your changes alter what it builds, say so plainly. Say which assumptions these choices replace.

Act on the proposal in docs/plans/ATMOSPHERE/LOG.md (2026-11-14, from SCENE-VIEWS' planner): the aerial pass stops a descending column at the model's ground, so observers near sea level read thin haze just above the horizon, and mirror views inherit it. Sea-level scenes (the sea, sunsets) are a showcase priority. Fix it in ATMOSPHERE's design and plan with the modern technique, keeping SCENE-VIEWS, WATERS and CLOUDS consistent, and say where exact baselines move.

Two tasks in one pass.
1) Dependency audit. The owner (14 Nov 2026) says development is far behind pace: Codex quota use is about 5% a day against a target near 15%, because only 4 milestones can start at once. Go through every milestone dependency in docs/plans/*/PLAN.md and DONE.json, and remove each edge that only sets an order, keeping only those where a milestone needs another milestone's actual output (code, interface, data or a verified baseline it builds on). Where a milestone needs only part of another, depend on the earliest milestone that provides that part. Owner decision: keep the swarm-game modules (SIM-2D, SWARM, TRANSPORT, RENDER-2D, GAME-UI, SESSION) gated on SHOWCASE:M8 as they are now. Contention for the shared GPU lock and disk is not a reason for an edge; the script queues GPU work. List each edge you removed or kept with a one-line reason in the evidence folder, and say how many milestones can start once the running ones finish.
2) ATMOSPHERE's latest design review (docs/evidence/ATMOSPHERE/design-review.md) found 1 Must Fix after the horizon-haze re-plan. Resolve it, keeping SCENE-VIEWS, WATERS and CLOUDS consistent.

Move Thrum onto the proof regime the owner approved, using orchestrate 2.3.1, in one pass, tonight.

Why: delivery stalled under proofs. In the last 24h, 4 milestones reached Ready for Review against 419 commits, and 163 of 288 background jobs failed. The single GPU lock was 92-94% busy, mostly with rebase, re-prove and merge attempts that failed. The design is in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ryannel-Workspace-thrum/e5ff9d25-dfb5-4b37-a169-158dbdac268c/scratchpad/proof-regime.md; section 4 has the steps T1a-T9. The script now does much of what it proposed: shared resources, lock hold limits, `reads`, a merge queue and main-branch checks with retry and bisect. Read ~/.claude/plugins/cache/ryannel-skills/orchestrate/2.3.1/skills/orchestration/build/SKILL.md, build-milestone/SKILL.md and plan-module/references/proofs.md before you change anything.

The owner's words, to quote wherever a change is the human's decision: "Ok, let's get the script and skill changes done then once we've got orchestrate to where it needs to be, let's get the lead on Thrum working." and "We want all these fixes in place before I head to bed tonight." The owner also confirmed "Go ahead" in the lead session on 15 Nov. That covered: a warning-only gate, an hourly verifier on main, `gpu: 2, chrome: 1`, BASELINE-GUARD re-planned, the rule and skill text updated, and accepting that an unintended image change can sit on main for about 2 hours.

Carry out, adjusted for 2.3.0:
- **T1a.** The exact-baselines gate in `./dev check` warns instead of refusing. Declare the verifier as a `Main-branch check` in ORCHESTRATE.md (every 1h; lock gpu; a timeout that fits the ~16 min run). Record a dated ruling in ARCHITECTURE.md's Exact baselines.
- **T1b.** The script now does the sentinel's shared run, retry, bisect and naming the culprit. Re-plan BASELINE-GUARD down to what remains Thrum's own (for example the verify command and the CPU ownership guard), and decide what happens to its in-flight M2 on branch build/baseline-guard.
- **Verifier items.** Open milestones carry about 116 items whose check runs `exact_baselines.py verify`. Changing `check` text resets progress, which `lock` and `reads` don't. Weigh repointing them at `python3 "$ORCHESTRATE_SCRIPT" main-check <name>` (no lock of its own) against having the verifier read the shared result. Pick the option that disturbs open branches least, and say why.
- **T2-T5,** as the report says. In T4, never nest gpu inside merge, and never hold a lock while waiting for a person.
- **T6.** Declare `Shared resources: gpu: 2, chrome: 1`; that capacity change is what ends most of the queueing. Give each item the lock its device needs for capacity. Use `gpu.alone` only for a run that needs the whole GPU, such as all its memory. It does not make timings trustworthy, because builders compiling elsewhere take no lock.
- **T9's timing policy is the timing fix.** Within a milestone, a timing item becomes a loose benchmark tripwire that catches a collapse. Precise numbers move to the module's last milestone, measured in one sitting with builders paused. Sweep the timing items to that line.
- **Fold T7-T8 in** where they're cheap; otherwise record them as later work.

Constraints:
- Don't edit the orchestrate skills or agent_loop.py. If the script blocks a step, stop that step and write down what happened.
- Keep open branches mergeable.
- Work in the lead worktree or your own; never touch the main checkout's tmp/.

Done when:
- the changes are merged to main, `./dev check-docs` passes and the plan checks pass;
- an open branch can merge without a fresh exact-image proof;
- the main-branch check is declared and `main-check --due` lists it;
- your report names the commits, every module whose design review is now owed, and anything you held back because it goes beyond what the owner approved.

Settle one design question for ATMOSPHERE before M7 is built. M7 makes haze a weather input, but only its amount: the aerosol is grey with one fixed phase lobe, so haze can only thicken and can't turn bluish when dry or whitish when humid. A review of three recent theses (tmp/theses/atmos-theses-review.md in this worktree, recommendation 1) proposes a second input, such as an Angstrom exponent or an aerosol type, defaulting to today's values so existing scenes don't change. It also touches CLOUDS' ruling 8. First check whether the colour change is visible in the existing reference sky at about 20 km and 3 km visual range; if it isn't, drop the idea and record why. If it is, decide whether and how ATMOSPHERE's design and M7 should change, resolve it with CLOUDS and any contract it touches, and route the change through design review as the orchestrate skills require. The owner asked for this check; the rest of the theses review needs no action now.

Owner decision, 17 Nov 2026: 'Ok let's lower the bar.' Thrum is a game engine; the aim is the most plausible result as fast as possible, not physical accuracy. New bar for rendering and visual work: it looks as good as shipped high-end games, judged against an agent-written visual inspection list, and it runs fast, with performance as tripwires (no invented budgets). Physical or f64 references stop being pass/fail gates: they stay as diagnostic tools used when output looks wrong, to find the cause. Exact image baselines stay only where they guard against unintended regressions, not to block deliberate shader changes. Correctness proofs stay where failures are silent and costly: networking and transport, simulation determinism, asset and cooked formats, contracts between modules. Also make proof proportional to risk: small fix rounds and tripwire records shouldn't get the same review weight as new rendering work, and cut evidence items that cost more than the risk they cover. Apply this to ORCHESTRATE.md, the thrum-engineering skill (.agents/skills/thrum-engineering), docs/design/AI-DEVELOPMENT.md and AI-PERFORMANCE.md where they set the bar, and every open module's DESIGN, PLAN and DONE.json for milestones not yet Done (CLOUDS's M3 two-stream model, ATMOSPHERE, WATERS, APPLE-PRESENTATION and so on): rewrite or drop items that gate on accuracy rather than look and speed. Milestones currently being built or Ready for Review keep their items unless an item is now clearly pointless; say which you changed in flight. Record the owner's decision and date where the settings record decisions. Don't change modules' scope or the V1 exit beyond the bar. Done when the settings, skill, design docs and done-when files say the new bar consistently, ./dev check-docs passes, and your report lists each module's dropped or rewritten items and an estimate of reviews and fix rounds saved.
